false_sentence: Why can a gecko climb straight up a polished glass window while a tree frog slides right off?
correct_version: Tree frogs cling to smooth glass very well: their toe pads use a thin film of mucus (wet adhesion) plus friction, which is why they are often seen on windows. Geckos use dry adhesion instead: millions of tiny hairs (setae) that split into billions of tips attracted to the surface by van der Waals forces. Both stick; they stick in different ways.
